## Q1
1.
```{r}
library(IMIFA)
class(olive)
```
Dataset is a data frame
```{r}
class(olive) <- c("mydf", class(olive))
class(olive)
```
 
2.
```{r}
print.mydf <- function(x, n = 5) {
  if(n > 5){
    stop("n must be <= 5")
}

  r <- min(n, nrow(x))
  c <- min(n, ncol(x))
  #in case dataset is smaller than n
  x <- x[1:r, 1:c]
  
  class(x) <- "data.frame"
  print(x)
}
print.mydf(olive)
```

3.
```{r}
print(olive[-1, ])
```
since method only prints at most 5 rows/columns, 
when we try to print all but the first row, we end up with rows 2-6

4.
```{r}
print.mydf <- function(x, n = 5) {
  if (n > nrow(x) || n > ncol(x)) {
    warning("n exceeds the number of rows or columns in the data frame")}

  r <- min(n, nrow(x))
  c <- min(n, ncol(x))
  #in case dataset is smaller than n
  message("Printing ", r, " rows and ", c, " cols.")

  x <- x[1:r, 1:c]
  
  class(x) <- "data.frame"
  print(x)}

print(olive, n = 100)
```

5.
```{r}
max_dens <- function(x, ...) {
  UseMethod("max_dens")}
#Create the generic max_dens()

max_dens.density <- function(x, ...) { #match arguements

  yMax <- max(x$y) #density paek
  xMax <- x$x[which.max(x$y)] #location of that peak

  c(y = yMax, x = xMax)}

max_dens(density(olive$palmitic))
```

6.
```{r}
#all numeric data
data <- olive |>
  select(palmitic, palmitoleic, stearic, oleic, linoleic, linolenic, arachidic, eicosenoic)

pmatrix <- vapply(data, 
                  function(x) {
                    dens <- density(x, kernel="epanechnikov")
                            max_dens(dens)},
                  numeric(2))
pmatrix
```

7.
```{r}
p <- density(olive$palmitic, kernel = "epanechnikov")
peak <- max_dens(p)

plot(dens)
segments(x0 = peak["x"], y0 = 0,
         x1 = peak["x"], y1 = peak["y"], col = "red")
```

## Q2
1.
```{r}
f <- function(x) {
  x + 3}

g <- function(x) {
  x^2 - 4}
```

2.
```{r}
curve(f, from = -4, to = 4, ylim = c(-6, 12))
curve(g, from = -4, to = 4, add = TRUE)
```

3.
```{r}
h <- function(x) {f(x) - g(x)} #roots when this = 0
r1 <- uniroot(h, interval = c(-4, 0), tol = 1e-08) #1st root
r2 <- uniroot(h, interval = c(2, 4), tol = 1e-08) #2nd root

r1$root; r2$root
```

4.
```{r}
farea <- integrate(f, lower = r1$root, upper = r2$root)
garea <- integrate(g, lower = r1$root, upper = r2$root)

farea$value - garea$value
```

## Q3
1.
```{r}
df <- with(mtcars, data.frame(y=mpg, x1=disp, x2=hp, x3=wt))
head(df)
```

2.
```{r}
nll_lm <- function(data, par){

  B <- par[1:4] #B0, B1, B2, B3
  sigma <- par[5]
  fitted <- B[1] + B[2]*data$x1 + B[3]*data$x2 + B[4]*data$x3

  resid <- data$y - fitted

  -sum(dnorm(resid, mean = 0, sd = sigma, log = TRUE))}
```

3.
```{r}
start <- c(mean(df$y), 0, 0, 0, sd(df$y))

low <- c(-Inf, -Inf, -Inf, -Inf, 1e-8) #sd cant be <= 0

up <- c(Inf, Inf, Inf, Inf, Inf)

fit <- optim(par = start, fn = nll_lm, data = df,
  method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = low, upper = up)

fit$par #B0, B1, B2, B3, sd
```

4.
We want to find the parameter values that maximise the likelihood.
optim() minimises a function.
Minimising negative log-likelihood gets same result as maximising the log-likelihood.

5.
```{r}
X <- cbind(1, df$x1, df$x2, df$x3)
y <- df$y

beta_m <- solve(t(X) %*% X) %*% t(X) %*% y
beta_m
```

6.
```{r}
fitted_m <- X %*% beta_m #predicted y for each row
resid_m <- y - fitted_m # e = y - XB

RSS <- sum(resid_m^2)
sqrt(RSS / nrow(df))
```

7.
The estimates for the coefficients are close because both methods use the same least squares matrix equation
They differ when estimating s.d because max likelihood divides RSS by total observations while the other divides by residual degrees of freedom 

8.
```{r}
fit <- optim(par = start, fn = nll_lm, data = df,
  method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = low, upper = up, hessian = TRUE)

H <- fit$hessian
cov_m <- solve(H)
sqrt(diag(cov_m)[1:4])
```
